subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A clerk found the average salary of 16 employees to be Rs 61 thousand, but he had typed one salary of Rs 49 thousand as Rs 65 thousand. What is the true average salary?
explanation: Correct total = 16 × 61 − 65 + 49 = 960; correct mean = 960/16 = 60.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average weight of 17 bags was noted as 45 kg. A bag weighing 39 kg was afterwards found to have been read as 5 kg. What is the actual average weight?
explanation: Correct total = 17 × 45 − 5 + 39 = 799; correct mean = 799/17 = 47.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A teacher found the class average to be 65 for 26 pupils. On checking, she saw that a score of 80 had been read as 54. The correct average is:
explanation: Correct total = 26 × 65 − 54 + 80 = 1716; correct mean = 1716/26 = 66.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean temperature over 15 days was reported as 21 °C, but one day’s reading of 36 °C had been copied as 66 °C. What is the correct mean temperature?
explanation: Correct total = 15 × 21 − 66 + 36 = 285; correct mean = 285/15 = 19.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 21 numbers is 74. Two of the numbers, 90 and 94, were wrongly taken as 58 and 84. What is the correct average?
explanation: The total must change by (90 + 94) − (58 + 84) = 42; correct mean = 74 + 42/21 = 76.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean height of 39 trainees was calculated as 173 cm. Two heights, 164 cm and 200 cm, had been recorded as 134 cm and 152 cm. What is the correct mean height?
explanation: The total must change by (164 + 200) − (134 + 152) = 78; correct mean = 173 + 78/39 = 175.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A scorer worked out the average runs of 17 batsmen as 46, having entered 34 for 60 and 40 for 48. What is the correct average?
explanation: The total must change by (60 + 48) − (34 + 40) = 34; correct mean = 46 + 34/17 = 48.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 16 numbers was calculated as 74. It was later found that the number 107 had been misread, and the correct average is 76. What value had been used by mistake?
explanation: The correction changed the total by 16 × (76 − 74) = 32; so the wrong value was 107 − 32 = 75.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 20 parcels were said to have an average weight of 40 kg. A parcel actually weighing 79 kg had been recorded wrongly, and the true average is 38 kg. What weight had been recorded for that parcel?
explanation: The correction changed the total by 20 × (38 − 40) = -40; so the wrong value was 79 + 40 = 119.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average score of 16 players was announced as 47. A score of 52 had been miscopied, and after correction the average is 48. What figure had been copied?
explanation: The correction changed the total by 16 × (48 − 47) = 16; so the wrong value was 52 − 16 = 36.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a class, the average marks of 39 boys are 40 and of 6 girls are 55. What is the average for the whole class?
explanation: Total = 39 × 40 + 6 × 55 = 1,890 for 45; average = 42 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: One section of 27 students has a mean age of 12 years and another of 9 students has a mean age of 16 years. Find the mean age of all the students.
explanation: Total = 27 × 12 + 9 × 16 = 468 for 36; average = 13 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A shop sold 27 shirts at an average price of Rs 1,100 and 18 shirts at an average price of Rs 900. What was the average price of all the shirts sold?
explanation: Total = 27 × 1,100 + 18 × 900 = 45,900 for 45; average = 1,020 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 24 workers earn Rs 1,100 a day on average and 36 others earn Rs 1,650 a day on average. What is the average daily wage of all the workers?
explanation: Total = 24 × 1,100 + 36 × 1,650 = 85,800 for 60; average = 1,430 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A batsman averaged 40 runs in his first 19 matches and 64 runs in the next 5. What is his average over all the matches?
explanation: Total = 19 × 40 + 5 × 64 = 1,080 for 24; average = 45 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A school’s 5 teachers have an average age of 42 years and its 9 other staff an average age of 28 years. What is the average age of all the staff?
explanation: Total = 5 × 42 + 9 × 28 = 462 for 14; average = 33 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A car covered an average of 47 km a day for 12 days and then 250 km a day for 9 days. What was its average daily distance?
explanation: Total = 12 × 47 + 9 × 250 = 2,814 for 21; average = 134 (not the simple mean of the two averages).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average salary of all the staff in an office is Rs 57,000. The 6 officers average Rs 85,000 and the clerks average Rs 54,000. How many clerks are there?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A class has an average score of 81. The 8 girls average 87 and the boys average 57. How many boys are in the class?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: In a factory the average wage is Rs 1,300 a day. The 6 skilled workers get Rs 2,700 on average and the unskilled workers Rs 900. How many unskilled workers are there?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 24 numbers is 28. The average of the first 21 of them is 26. What is the average of the remaining numbers?
explanation: Total = 24 × 28 = 672; first 21 total = 546; rest = 126 over 3, average 42.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A team of 12 players has an average age of 29 years. If the 10 senior players average 21 years, what is the average age of the others?
explanation: Total = 12 × 29 = 348; first 10 total = 210; rest = 138 over 2, average 69.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 5 consecutive integers is 52. What is the largest of them?
explanation: The average of equally spaced numbers is the middle value; with 5 terms 1 apart, the largest is 52 + 2 = 54.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of 3 consecutive even numbers is 54. What is the smallest of them?
explanation: The average of equally spaced numbers is the middle value; with 3 terms 2 apart, the smallest is 54 − 2 = 52.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 7 consecutive odd numbers have an average of 47. Find the greatest of them.
explanation: The average of equally spaced numbers is the middle value; with 7 terms 2 apart, the largest is 47 + 6 = 53.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The ages of 5 cousins are consecutive odd numbers whose average is 13 years. How old is the youngest cousin?
explanation: The average of equally spaced numbers is the middle value; with 5 terms 2 apart, the smallest is 13 − 4 = 9.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 3 consecutive multiples of 5 is 10. What is the largest of these multiples?
explanation: The average of equally spaced numbers is the middle value; with 3 terms 5 apart, the largest is 10 + 5 = 15.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the average of all the even numbers from 52 to 86, both included?
explanation: Equally spaced numbers: average = (52 + 86)/2 = 69.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Find the average of the first 86 natural numbers.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: What is the mean of all the odd numbers between 8 and 84?
explanation: The odd numbers run from 9 to 83; average = (9 + 83)/2 = 46.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average age of 5 children born at intervals of 4 years each is 25 years. How old is the youngest child?
explanation: The ages are equally spaced, so the average is the middle age; the youngest is 25 − (5 − 1) × 4/2 = 17.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 5 saplings were planted in a row, one every 2 days, and today their average age is 44 days. How old is the oldest sapling?
explanation: The ages are equally spaced, so the average is the middle age; the eldest is 44 + (5 − 1) × 2/2 = 48.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 6 numbers in arithmetic progression with common difference 2 is 24. What is the largest of them?
explanation: The ages are equally spaced, so the average is the middle age; the eldest is 24 + (6 − 1) × 2/2 = 29.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: 4 brothers were born at intervals of 4 years, and their average age today is 22 years. How old is the eldest brother?
explanation: The ages are equally spaced, so the average is the middle age; the eldest is 22 + (4 − 1) × 4/2 = 28.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The sum of 5 consecutive odd numbers is 235. Which is the smallest of them?
explanation: Average = 235/5 = 47, the middle number; the smallest is 47 − 4 = 43.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The total of 7 consecutive even numbers is 364. What is their average?
explanation: Average = 364/7 = 52, the middle number; so the average is 52.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of a set of numbers is 62. If 11 is added to each number, what is the new mean?
explanation: Adding 11 to every value adds 11 to the mean: 62 + 11 = 73.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average age of a group of friends is 23 years. What will their average age be after 2 years?
explanation: Adding 2 to every value adds 2 to the mean: 23 + 2 = 25.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Every employee in an office gets a raise of Rs 1,000. If the average salary was Rs 77,000 before the raise, what is it now?
explanation: Adding 1,000 to every value adds 1,000 to the mean: 77,000 + 1,000 = 78,000.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Every price in a shop is raised by 20%. If the average price of its goods was Rs 800, what is the new average price?
explanation: Raising every value by 20% raises the mean by 20%: 800 × 120/100 = 960.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of some numbers is 8. If each number is multiplied by 6, what is the new average?
explanation: Multiplying every value by 6 multiplies the mean by 6: 8 × 6 = 48.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of a data set is 81. If 12 is subtracted from each value, the new mean is:
explanation: Subtracting 12 from every value lowers the mean by 12: 81 − 12 = 69.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Each of the 22 marks in a test is reduced by 4 as a penalty for late submission. If the average mark was 40, what is the new average?
explanation: Subtracting 4 from every value lowers the mean by 4: 40 − 4 = 36.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of a list of numbers is 114. If every number is divided by 2, what does the average become?
explanation: Dividing every value by 2 divides the mean by 2: 114/2 = 57.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The mean of 21 numbers is 75. If each number is doubled and then increased by 11, what is the new mean?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of a set of scores is 82. Each score is halved and then 7 is added to it. What is the new average?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of 7 numbers is 44. The average of the first 4 is 58 and that of the last 4 is 32. What is the 4th number?
explanation: First 4 total + last 4 total = 232 + 128 = 360; this counts the 4th value twice, and all 7 total 308; so the 4th value = 360 − 308 = 52.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A cricketer’s average over 13 innings is 47. His average in the first 7 innings was 43, and in the last 7 it was 49. How many runs did he make in the 7th innings?
explanation: First 7 total + last 7 total = 301 + 343 = 644; this counts the 7th value twice, and all 13 total 611; so the 7th value = 644 − 611 = 33.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Over 9 days a shop’s average daily sale was Rs 4,300. The average for the first 5 days was Rs 3,800 and for the last 5 days Rs 5,000. What was the sale on the 5th day?
explanation: First 5 total + last 5 total = 19000 + 25000 = 44000; this counts the 5th value twice, and all 9 total 38700; so the 5th value = 44000 − 38700 = 5300.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average temperature for a week was 30 °C. The average of the first four days was 35 °C and that of the last four days was 25 °C. What was the temperature on the fourth day?
explanation: First 4 total + last 4 total = 140 + 100 = 240; this counts the 4th value twice, and all 7 total 210; so the 4th value = 240 − 210 = 30.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A student’s average mark in 7 subjects is 77. Her average in the first 4 subjects is 63 and in the last 4 subjects is 88. What did she score in the 4th subject?
explanation: First 4 total + last 4 total = 252 + 352 = 604; this counts the 4th value twice, and all 7 total 539; so the 4th value = 604 − 539 = 65.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average age of the 7 members of a team is 28 years. The first 4 members on the list average 24 years and the last 4 average 32 years. How old is the member in the middle of the list?
explanation: First 4 total + last 4 total = 96 + 128 = 224; this counts the 4th value twice, and all 7 total 196; so the 4th value = 224 − 196 = 28.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average weight of Saba and Bilal is 68 kg, of Bilal and Ali is 51 kg, and of Saba and Ali is 63 kg. How much does Saba weigh?
explanation: Sum of all three = 68 + 51 + 63 = 182; subtract twice the pair average that excludes the required one: 182 − 102 = 80.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average of x and y is 53, of y and z is 57, and of x and z is 64. What is the average of x, y and z?
explanation: Adding the three pair averages gives (2x + 2y + 2z)/2 = x + y + z = 174; the average of the three = 174/3 = 58.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: The average monthly income of P and Q is Rs 43,000, of Q and R is Rs 32,000, and of P and R is Rs 48,000. What is Q’s income?
explanation: Sum of all three = 43000 + 32000 + 48000 = 123000; subtract twice the pair average that excludes the required one: 123000 − 96000 = 27000.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A batsman has an average of 39 runs after 10 innings. How many runs must he score in the next innings to raise his average to 44?
explanation: Needed total = 11 × 44 = 484; present total = 10 × 39 = 390; next value = 94.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Ayesha’s average in 11 tests is 65 marks. What must she score in the next test to lift her average to 69?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 69 = 828; present total = 11 × 65 = 715; next value = 113.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A salesman has averaged 29 sales a day for 11 days. How many sales must he make tomorrow to bring his average up to 31?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 31 = 372; present total = 11 × 29 = 319; next value = 53.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A farmer’s wheat yield has averaged 40 maunds per acre over 7 acres. What yield must the next acre give to make the average 42 maunds per acre?
explanation: Needed total = 8 × 42 = 336; present total = 7 × 40 = 280; next value = 56.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A batsman scores 81 runs in his 18th innings and thereby increases his average by 2. What is his average after this innings?
explanation: Let the new average be A. Then 17(A − 2) + 81 = 18A ⇒ A = 81 − 17 × 2 = 47; the earlier average was 45.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: By scoring 121 in the 21st match of the season, a player raised his average by 4 runs. What was his average before that match?
explanation: Let the new average be A. Then 20(A − 4) + 121 = 21A ⇒ A = 121 − 20 × 4 = 41; the earlier average was 37.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A student’s average rose by 2 marks when she scored 84 in her 7th test. What is her new average?
explanation: Let the new average be A. Then 6(A − 2) + 84 = 7A ⇒ A = 84 − 6 × 2 = 72; the earlier average was 70.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bowler’s average is 30 runs per wicket. He takes 4 wickets for 74 runs in his next match, and his average falls by 1. How many wickets had he taken before this match?

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bowler who had been conceding 30 runs per wicket took 5 wickets for 54 runs in a match, which lowered his average by 1. How many wickets has he taken in all now?
explanation: If he had w wickets: (30w + 54)/(w + 5) = 29 ⇒ 1w = 150 − 5 − 54 ⇒ w = 91; now he has 96.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A student needs an average of 72 marks over 12 papers to win a scholarship. In the first 6 papers she averaged 68. What average does she need in the remaining papers?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 72 = 864; achieved = 6 × 68 = 408; the rest 6 must average 456/6 = 76.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A shop wants average daily sales of Rs 69,000 over 12 days. It averaged Rs 63,000 in the first 4 days. What must it average over the remaining days?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 69,000 = 828,000; achieved = 4 × 63,000 = 252,000; the rest 8 must average 576,000/8 = 72,000.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A team must score at an average of 7 runs per over in a 12-over innings. In the first 6 overs it scored at 6 runs per over. What rate is needed in the remaining overs?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 7 = 84; achieved = 6 × 6 = 36; the rest 6 must average 48/6 = 8.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A factory must average 330 units a day over 7 days to meet an order. It averaged 280 units a day in the first 2 days. What daily average is needed for the rest of the period?
explanation: Needed total = 7 × 330 = 2,310; achieved = 2 × 280 = 560; the rest 5 must average 1,750/5 = 350.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: An athlete wants to average 9 km a day over 12 days of training. For the first 8 days she averaged 8 km. What must she average over the remaining days?
explanation: Needed total = 12 × 9 = 108; achieved = 8 × 8 = 64; the rest 4 must average 44/4 = 11.

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A shopkeeper buys a table for Rs 4,200 and sells it for Rs 4,704. What is his profit percentage?
explanation: Profit = Rs 504; profit % = 504/4,200 × 100 = 12% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A dealer bought a motorcycle for Rs 116,000 and sold it for Rs 121,800. His percentage gain is:
explanation: Profit = Rs 5,800; profit % = 5,800/116,000 × 100 = 5% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Goods costing Rs 47,000 were sold for Rs 56,400. Find the gain percent.
explanation: Profit = Rs 9,400; profit % = 9,400/47,000 × 100 = 20% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A trader buys a bag of rice for Rs 7,100 and sells it for Rs 8,165. What percentage profit does he earn?
explanation: Profit = Rs 1,065; profit % = 1,065/7,100 × 100 = 15% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: Hamza bought a goat for Rs 118,000 before Eid and sold it for Rs 153,400. What percentage profit did he make?
explanation: Profit = Rs 35,400; profit % = 35,400/118,000 × 100 = 30% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A bookseller pays Rs 1,780 for a dictionary and charges Rs 2,314 for it. What is his profit as a percentage of cost?
explanation: Profit = Rs 534; profit % = 534/1,780 × 100 = 30% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A mobile phone bought for Rs 55,000 was sold for Rs 68,750. What was the rate of profit?
explanation: Profit = Rs 13,750; profit % = 13,750/55,000 × 100 = 25% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A used car bought for Rs 2,868,000 was sold for Rs 2,523,840. What is the loss percentage?
explanation: Loss = Rs 344,160; loss % = 344,160/2,868,000 × 100 = 12% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A trader sold a refrigerator for Rs 117,000 that had cost him Rs 130,000. What was his percentage loss?
explanation: Loss = Rs 13,000; loss % = 13,000/130,000 × 100 = 10% (always on cost price).

subject: Quantitative Ability
q: A farmer bought a buffalo for Rs 367,000 but had to sell it for Rs 183,500. What percentage did he lose?

explanation: Loss = Rs 2,100; loss % = 2,100/42,000 × 100 = 5% (always on cost price).

q: A shopkeeper cleared old stock that had cost Rs 61,000 by selling it for Rs 54,900. What was his loss as a percentage of cost?
